title: Cech cup products and pullback
statement: Let f:X' \to X be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let U be an arbitrary open cover of X, and let U' be an open cover of X' together with a specified refinement map U' \to f^{-1}U in the sense of Stacks Tag 01FD. Let F and G be quasi-coherent modules on X [pqf-def-coherent], and write f^*F and f^*G for their pullbacks to X' [def-pc-module-pullback]. (a) The refinement cochain map from the Cech complex of (X,U,F) to that of (X',U',f^*F) is compatible with the usual pullback map H^p(X,F) \to H^p(X',f^*F) under the canonical maps from Cech cohomology to cohomology, \check H^p(U,F) \to H^p(X,F) and \check H^p(U',f^*F) \to H^p(X',f^*F), which exist for every open cover. (b) For an arbitrary open cover U of X, the signed Cech cup-product cochain map of Tag 07MB, Tot(Cech(U,F) \otimes Cech(U,G)) \to Cech(U,F\otimes G), induces on cohomology a map \check H^p(U,F) \otimes \check H^q(U,G) \to \check H^{p+q}(U,F\otimes G) that is compatible with the sheaf cup product H^p(X,F) \otimes H^q(X,G) \to H^{p+q}(X,F\otimes G) under the canonical maps \check H^n(U,-) \to H^n(X,-) (Stacks Tag 0FKV, cohomology-lemma-diagrams-commute); in particular, when these canonical maps are isomorphisms (for instance for a finite affine cover of a scheme with affine diagonal and quasi-coherent F, G), the Cech cup product is the sheaf cup product. Both assertions are natural in F,G and f.

source.place: Tags 01FD (cohomology-lemma-functoriality-cech), 07MB (cohomology-equation-needs-signs) and 0FKV (cohomology-lemma-diagrams-commute: the signed Cech cup product is compatible with the cup product on RGamma via the canonical maps, for every open covering)

proof.text: Apply cechRefinement_comparison_square [lem-sc-cech-refinement-comparison-square] to the given canonical comparisons and specified refinement. This is exactly the first conjunct, without any comparison-isomorphism hypothesis.

For the two Cech complexes and the sheaf tensor product, form the total tensor complex using d(a tensor b)=d(a) tensor b+(-1)^(deg a) a tensor d(b). The Cech cup map of Tag 07MB restricts the two factors to common intersections and inserts the total-complex signs; expanding the alternating restriction differential gives the Leibniz identity, with omitted-vertex terms cancelling in adjacent pairs. For sheaves in degree zero this specializes to the ordinary Cech cup product.

Lift the two Cech homology classes to kernel cocycles using surjectivity of the cycle-class map (Mathlib ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective and the homology projection). Leibniz constructs their cup cocycle [def-sc-cech-cup-product]. Apply cechCup_resolution_representatives [lem-sc-cech-cup-resolution-representatives] to obtain a computing pairing and global cocycles whose three classes are the canonical images. The characterizations IsCechCupProduct and IsModuleCupProduct [def-sc-module-cohomology-cup-product] then identify the two products. When all comparisons are isomorphisms, apply injectivity of cFG to the product equality evaluated on the two inverse images; inv_hom_id cancels the comparisons.

The refinement map in Step 1 carries a cup cochain to the cup cochain of the pulled-back factors: on each intersection this is f^*(s tensor t)=f^*s tensor f^*t, and the total-complex sign depends only on the degrees. Thus the refinement square commutes with the cup map. Combining this identity with Step 3 proves compatibility of cup products with pullback. The same restriction and tensor identities commute with morphisms of F and G, and refinement functions compose, proving naturality. The Lean delivery V3 proves three naturality declarations directly: cech_coefficient_apply transports a coefficient morphism through the Cech product projections and the intersection equivalence. Unit naturality and Hom.app_presheaf_map then prove cechRefinement_coefficient_naturality. For cechCup_coefficient_naturality, first prove the cochain coefficient identity by tensorHom_app_tmulSection and restriction naturality. Represent both homology classes by concrete kernel cycles (the cycle-class map is an epimorphism). Leibniz gives their cup cycle. Transport cycles and cycle classes along the cochain coefficient maps using Mathlib cyclesMap_i and homologypi_naturality, and apply the IsCechCupProduct characterization to the source and target cycles. Finally, cechCup_refinement_naturality follows tuplewise from the section formula of lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor, tensor-section restriction, and the unit restriction square on each front/back face. The resolution comparisons are reduced to the two D4 intermediate statements. Q4 proves the sheaf-cup naturalities in the additional steps below using existing compatible computing resolutions. The successive-refinement composition is formalized in the next step. B2 uses the specified canonical comparisons directly; their separate existence theorem is not needed in this module.

R3 proves cechRefinement_composition_naturality without new intermediate holes. The definition tensorSectionsComp in [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial] is the conjugate of pushforwardComp; Mathlib unit_conjugateEquiv_symm gives its adjunction-unit equation. On each tuple of refined indices expand the two IsCechRefinementMap formulas [def-sc-cech-refinement-cochain-map]. Naturality of the second adjunction unit moves the first restriction through it. Compose the resulting restrictions in the presheaf, move the coefficient comparison through the last restriction, and evaluate the conjugate-unit equation on the original intersection section. Injectivity of the tuple equivalence proves the cochain-composition equality. For the composite comparison square, B2 applies cechRefinement_comparison_square [lem-sc-cech-refinement-comparison-square] directly to the given comparisons and composite refinement. No auxiliary canonical comparisons or cup products are chosen. Apply Mathlib homologyMap_comp to the cochain equality and mapHomologyIso_hom_naturality to its final coefficient map. Cancel the intermediate forgetting-scalars homology isomorphisms to identify the threefold homology composite with the composite refinement homology map. The existing composite refinement comparison gives the second conjunct. Finally the adjunction-unit equation is exactly the hypothesis of moduleCohomologyPullback_comp in [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-functorial], which gives the third conjunct. This uses the existing refinement comparison square as a tool and introduces no circular dependency.

proof.text: For coefficient naturality, obtain compatible computing pairings D and E and three coefficient cochain maps from moduleCup_coefficient_resolution_maps. The cycle projection is surjective, and the global comparison and injective-resolution identification are isomorphisms, so each resolution class map is surjective. Lift both input cohomology classes to concrete kernel cycles of D. Its signed Leibniz identity constructs their product cycle. Transport all three cycles along the global-sections cochain maps using Mathlib cyclesMap. The moduleCatCyclesIso equations identify the underlying sections. The supplied strict pairing square identifies the transported product cycle with the product of the transported input cycles. Apply IsModuleCupProduct to D and E and rewrite by the three supplied resolution-class equations to obtain moduleCup_coefficient_naturality.

proof.text: For pullback naturality obtain compatible computing pairings D and E and additive global cochain maps over the three pullback coefficient maps from moduleCup_pullback_resolution_maps. Lift the two input classes to D-kernel cycles and construct their product cycle by the preceding surjectivity and Leibniz arguments. For any additive cochain map between module complexes with possibly different rings, its degree map carries a concrete kernel cycle to a kernel cycle: evaluate its chain-map equation on that section, then use the source differential vanishing and preservation of zero. This is a genuine explicit kernel construction, requiring no linearity over a common ring. Apply it to the three supplied maps. Their strict pairing equation gives the transported product identity. Rewrite the source cup by its characterization in D, use the three resolution-class equations (the target one includes the normalized tensor-pullback coefficient comparison), and apply the target cup characterization in E. This proves moduleCup_pullback_naturality with its existing signature and no comparison-isomorphism or flatness hypothesis.

proof_origin.place: Tags 01FD, 07MB and 0FKV; V3 formalizes the coefficient and refinement naturalities of Step 4 using the existing section-normalized tensor-pullback theorem and the Cech Leibniz theorem, with explicit kernel-to-homology transports; R3 formalizes successive-refinement composition by the conjugate-unit equation, tuplewise restriction naturality, homology functoriality, and the existing cohomology-pullback composition theorem; B2 simplifies its comparison-square conjunct to a direct application of cechRefinement_comparison_square and removes the unused canonical-comparison existence dependency; D4 reduces the comparison and cup conjuncts to a refinement comparison square and compatible resolution representatives, and proves the inverse clause by injectivity.; Q4 proves the two remaining sheaf-cup naturality declarations from existing coefficient and pullback resolution maps, with explicit kernel-cycle transport, surjectivity of computing class maps, and the two cup-product characterizations; no new theorem holes.
